summary:
SPACE RELIC is an interactive digital museum and open historical engineering archive dedicated to humanity's forgotten, inactive, and stranded space exploration hardware. 

Rather than adopting generic sci-fi tropes, Space Relic applies museum-grade editorial design to document extraterrestrial archaeology across the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space. Sourced strictly from verified NASA NSSDCA, JPL, and ESA historical records, the platform features 10 landmark hardware entries (including Apollo 11's descent stage and EASEP, Opportunity, Lunokhod 1, and Philae) alongside an interactive spacecraft power-management simulator. 

The simulator teaches aerospace trade-offs between solar irradiance, dust opacity, thermal heating, battery reserves, and automated bus load-shedding during planetary storms. Space Relic preserves humanity’s off-world cultural heritage, educating the public on hardware longevity and the technical triumphs that carried humankind into the cosmos.
details:
What It Does:

SPACE RELIC is an interactive digital museum documenting the robotic landers, rovers, seismic packages, and descent stages abandoned across the Solar System. The platform features:

1. The Archive: A responsive catalog with debounced real-time search (by name, mission, coordinate, or year), multi-category filtering, and persistent URL routing.

2. Verified Hardware Records: Detailed technical narratives for 10 historical spacecraft, each featuring an interactive engineering component drawer (documenting power, mechanical, sensors, communication, and control subsystems), mission milestones, scientific discoveries, and a physical "What Remains?" condition table.

3. Engineering Lab: An interactive spacecraft power-management simulator implementing pure mathematical models of photovoltaic generation, solar angle, atmospheric dust opacity, battery depth-of-discharge, and autonomous subsystem load-shedding.

4. Chronological Timeline: Decade-grouped mission progression with dynamic distribution analytics.

Intended Impact & Benefits:

As lunar and Martian exploration enters an era of commercial traffic, early landing sites risk physical disruption or historical neglect. Space Relic treats abandoned hardware as monumental archaeology. It bridges technical aerospace engineering and public science communication, demonstrating how materials degrade under extreme cosmic conditions and why power budgets drive mission lifespans.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software:

• Framework: React 19 with TypeScript (strict mode) and Vite

• Styling & Design System: Tailwind CSS with 1px border architecture and custom font pairing (Space Grotesk, Inter, IBM Plex Mono)

• Motion & Transitions: Framer Motion (with prefers-reduced-motion accessibility support)

• Data Visualizations: Recharts (live battery and wattage area/line graphs, mission distribution charts)

• Routing: React Router with client-side SPA configuration

• Deployment & Infrastructure: Vercel Production with automated SPA rewrite rules (vercel.json)

Creativity & Design Factors:

Instead of standard sci-fi glow effects or dense data dashboards, Space Relic adopts a minimalist, archival aesthetic inspired by NASA historical documentation, technical blueprints, and Apple editorial sites. To preserve archival integrity, undocumented components never render, and missing media displays architectural schematic placeholders with public-domain photo credits rather than broken layouts.
